transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess the main thing is I’m having a really hard time keeping my mind on a task long enough to finish it. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s gotten pretty frustrating.

Like at work, I’ll be trying to trace a client’s network problem, and then ten minutes later I realize I’ve reread the same log entries three times and still don’t really know what they said. Even when it’s important, I just… lose the thread. Does that make sense?
Has this trouble focusing been something you've dealt with since childhood, or is this a new change for you, like something that started in the past few months?

No, it’s not really new. I mean, I’ve probably gotten better at covering for it as an adult, or at least trying to.

My mother still teases me that even in grade school my report cards were always like, “bright kid, but doesn’t stay in his seat,” or I’d blurt out answers, lose homework even when I’d actually done it… that kind of thing. So I guess it’s been there a long time. Does that answer what you mean?
How has your sleep been lately—do you feel rested when you wake up, or do you often feel excessively sleepy or tired during the day regardless of how much you sleep?

I’m not sure I have a great answer to that. I mean, I don’t think I’m falling asleep during the day or anything like that. I wake up… okay, I guess? Some mornings better than others.

I haven’t really been tracking it closely, so I don’t want to overstate it. I wouldn’t say I feel excessively sleepy regardless of sleep, at least not that I’ve noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Aside from the trouble focusing, have you noticed yourself feeling excessively worried or on edge about various things in your daily life, even when there's no clear reason to be?

I don’t think so… not in that way. I mean, I worry about normal things, like whether I’m keeping up at work or if I forgot something, but I wouldn’t say I’m just on edge all the time for no reason.

At least, I haven’t really thought of myself that way. Is that the distinction you’re getting at?
Do you currently notice yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble sitting still, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Yeah… I guess I do notice that. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but even when I’m supposed to be sitting still and listening, there’s this kind of… motor feeling, almost like a humming under my skin.

Like I need to get up, check something, or move on to the next problem right away. I try not to be disruptive, but internally it’s hard to just sit there and be still. Does that make sense?
Do you notice these same difficulties—trouble focusing, restlessness, or acting impulsively—affecting other areas of your life, like at home or in your relationships, not just at work?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say it’s mostly just work, but that probably wouldn’t be totally honest.

Since I lost the structure of my old job, it’s kind of spilled over. My reputation has taken a real hit. I’ve lost some freelance clients because I didn’t follow through the way they expected, and I missed out on a senior service-manager role, which… I guess I’m still pretty embarrassed about.

At home, my wife and I have had to worry more about money, partly because people don’t really trust me to follow through like they used to. I don’t mean I’m careless on purpose or anything, but it has affected more than just the office. Does that answer what you’re asking?

Have you ever had distinct periods lasting several days where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and had racing thoughts—different from your usual self?

No… I don’t think so. I’ve definitely had times where I’m wound up or irritable, but not like several days of feeling euphoric or like I suddenly don’t need sleep.

If anything, when I sleep less, I usually feel worse, not better. I don’t think I’ve had that kind of “different from myself” period you’re describing. Does that sound like what you mean?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or lost interest in things you'd normally enjoy?

I don’t think so… not in a steady, persistent way. I mean, I have moments where I feel discouraged or disappointed, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been sad most of the day or unable to enjoy things.

I’m not sure if I’m answering that the right way, but it doesn’t feel like a constant low mood over the past couple weeks.

Both symptom clusters are present concurrently, are pervasive across multiple settings (work, home, relationships), and have caused significant functional impairment (job loss, damaged professional reputation, financial strain).
